identity_dimensions: superstructure massing and how it sits on the hull

environments.label: Design studio
environments.prompt: A naval architect's design office: drawing boards, large pinned elevation sheets, screens showing line plans, a wide desk with rolled drawings, daylight from tall windows.

environments.label: Shipyard hall
environments.prompt: The interior of a shipbuilding assembly hall: steel roof trusses, an overhead travelling crane on its rails, a marked building berth with support blocks in a straight row, work platforms and staged steel plate, high side windows.

environments.label: Paint shed
environments.prompt: The interior of an enclosed fairing and paint shed: sealed white walls, even diffuse lighting from ceiling banks, mobile scaffolding towers, masking sheets and extraction ducting, no daylight.

environments.label: Launch quay
environments.prompt: A shipyard launch quay at the water's edge under open sky: concrete apron with bollards and mooring lines, a travel lift or quayside crane, calm harbour water, yard sheds in the distance.

environments.label: Open water
environments.prompt: Open sea under open sky, nothing but water to the horizon: moderate swell, natural daylight, no land, no harbour, no structure of any kind.

environments.label: At anchor
environments.prompt: A sheltered anchorage in daylight: calm water, a low coastline in the far distance, no other vessels close by, no harbour structures.

environments.label: Exterior deck aboard
environments.prompt: An open deck aboard the vessel: teak or composite decking, stainless guardrails, the sea visible beyond the rail, daylight from open sky.

environments.label: Interior space aboard
environments.prompt: An interior space aboard the vessel: full-height glazing to one side with the sea beyond, flush joinery, indirect ceiling light, no visible fixtures that would read as a building.

state_change_means: Either the stage of construction the vessel has reached, or the way a space aboard transforms in use.
scale_anchor: One standing person at distance. Without one in frame, a superyacht reads at any size.
